changes.title: Digital Operational Resilience Act: ICT risk management framework, dependency identification and ICT third-party register of information
changes.issuing_body: European Parliament and Council of the European Union

application_events.applies_to: All in-scope financial entities: general date of application of DORA obligations, including the ICT risk management framework and ICT third-party register of information

changes.change_summary: Article 6 requires financial entities to put in place, maintain and regularly review a comprehensive ICT risk management framework covering identification, protection/prevention, detection, response/recovery and learning/evolving capabilities, proportionate to their nature, scale and complexity. Article 8 requires identification, classification and documentation of all critical or important functions, the information and ICT assets supporting them, and mapping of dependencies between ICT assets, systems and processes. Article 28(1) requires the management body to adopt a dedicated strategy on ICT third-party risk addressing identification and management of all ICT third-party dependencies. Article 28(9) requires financial entities to maintain and keep up to date, at entity, sub-consolidated and consolidated level, a register of information on all contractual arrangements with ICT third-party service providers.

notes: Articles 6, 8, 28(1) and 28(9) text confirmed via direct EUR-Lex fetch; entry-into-force/application dates corroborated but not quote-verified against Article 64 itself (see source notes).

missing_evidence.reason: The 2023-01-16 entry-into-force date is corroborated by secondary sources and the standard 20-day rule applied to the 2022-12-27 publication date, but Article 64's own text was not quoted directly in this research session.
missing_evidence.required_input: Direct confirmation of Article 64 text against the EUR-Lex primary source

changes.title: EBA Guidelines on the management of ESG risks

application_events.applies_to: Institutions other than small and non-complex institutions (SNCIs)
Small and non-complex institutions (SNCIs) - latest application date
Competent authorities: deadline to notify the EBA of compliance or intended compliance, or reasons for non-compliance
application_events.locator: Guidelines, Section 1 'Compliance and reporting obligations', paragraph 3

changes.change_summary: Issued under Article 16 of Regulation (EU) No 1093/2010 pursuant to the mandate in Articles 87a(1), 87a(5) and 74 of Directive 2013/36/EU (CRD), these comply-or-explain guidelines set minimum standards and reference methodologies for institutions' identification, measurement, management and monitoring of environmental, social and governance (ESG) risks, including materiality assessment, data processes, integration into risk management (risk appetite, credit/market/liquidity/operational/reputational/concentration risk policies), and the content of Article 76(2) CRD transition plans. They apply to institutions other than SNCIs from 11 January 2026 and to SNCIs at the latest from 11 January 2027.

notes: Paragraphs 5, 8, 10 quoted directly from the official final-report PDF via pdftotext extraction.

changes.title: FRTB market-risk own-funds framework under CRR3: small trading-book-business exemption and repeatedly deferred application timeline
changes.legal_instrument_id: Regulation (EU) 2024/1623 amending Regulation (EU) No 575/2013 (CRR3), market risk own-funds requirements (Part Three, Title IV)
changes.issuing_body: European Parliament and Council of the European Union; European Commission (delegated acts under Article 461a CRR)

application_events.applies_to: CRR3 general date of application (most provisions other than market risk, which follows the Article 461a deferral chain below)
application_events.locator: Regulation (EU) 2024/1623, Article 3 (entry into force and application)

application_events.applies_to: FRTB alternative approaches for market-risk own funds requirements - date set by the first Article 461a delegated act (now superseded by the 2027-01-01 date below)

FRTB alternative approaches for market-risk own funds requirements - currently governing date under the second Article 461a delegated act; until this date institutions continue to apply the market-risk framework as it stood on 2024-07-08

Temporary targeted operational-relief measures and targeted multiplier for market-risk own funds requirements, proposed to apply from 2027-01-01 until 2030-01-01 - confirmed still under EP/Council scrutiny (not in force) as of 2026-08-03, roughly one month before the 2026-09-05 research cut-off; status for the remaining window to the cut-off is unresolved
application_events.locator: Draft/adopted Commission Delegated Regulation C(2026) 3647 final ('EU Market Risk Delegated Act'), not yet assigned an OJ CELEX number in the sources reviewed

changes.change_summary: CRR3 restructured own-funds requirements for market risk around the Basel III Fundamental Review of the Trading Book (FRTB). Two mechanisms are in scope for this dataset: (1) Article 94 CRR's long-standing 'derogation for small trading book business', which lets institutions below defined thresholds apply credit-risk rather than market-risk treatment to trading-book positions; and (2) the Article 461a CRR empowerment, under which the Commission has twice deferred the application date of the FRTB alternative approaches (first to 2026-01-01 via Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/2795, then to 2027-01-01 via Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/1496), and has adopted (4 June 2026, pending an EP/Council non-objection period) a further delegated act introducing temporary targeted adjustments rather than another outright postponement, since the two-year maximum deferral under Article 461a had already been used. The current legal status of that most recent delegated act was not resolved as of the research cut-off.

notes: Held at needs_review because the currently governing application date and the status of the pending 2026 delegated act could not be confirmed against a directly quoted primary text as of the research cut-off; this reflects genuine, currently-unsettled EU regulatory status rather than incomplete research effort.

Two-source corroboration applied for the 2027-01-01 date: EC news page and EBA statement PDF independently confirm the 2025-06-12 delegated act. A third, dated EBA source (SRC-FRTB-EBA-3RDFRTBDA-2026, 2026-08-03) narrows the pending 2026 act's unresolved window to 2026-08-03 through the 2026-09-05 cut-off.

missing_evidence.reason: SRC-FRTB-EBA-3RDFRTBDA-2026 (dated 2026-08-03) confirms the Commission Delegated Regulation adopted 2026-06-04 (C(2026) 3647 final) was still under EP/Council scrutiny and not in force as of that date, about one month before the research cut-off. Whether it completed scrutiny, was published in the Official Journal, or entered into force between 2026-08-03 and 2026-09-05 could not be confirmed from the sources reviewed.
missing_evidence.required_input: A current EUR-Lex or Official Journal record for this delegated regulation, or an EBA/EC statement confirming its status after the non-objection period

missing_evidence.reason: Article 94 CRR's exact current paragraph numbering and whether it has been renumbered or materially altered by CRR2/CRR3 (as distinct from the related Article 325a 'main risk driver' threshold mechanism) was not confirmed against primary text.
missing_evidence.required_input: Direct EUR-Lex confirmation of the current consolidated text of Article 94 CRR

changes.title: Instant credit transfers in euro: send/receive obligation, charges parity, verification of payee and sanctions screening
changes.issuing_body: European Parliament and Council of the European Union

application_events.applies_to: Euro-area PSPs: receive instant credit transfers; charges-parity obligation; sanctions-screening obligation
application_events.locator: Article 5a(8), Article 5b(3), Article 5d(3) (as inserted into Regulation (EU) No 260/2012)

application_events.applies_to: Euro-area PSPs: send instant credit transfers; Verification of Payee service
Non-euro-area PSPs: receive instant credit transfers; charges-parity obligation
Euro-area payment institutions and electronic money institutions: send and receive instant credit transfers
Non-euro-area PSPs: send instant credit transfers and Verification of Payee service; non-euro-area payment/e-money institutions: send obligation

changes.change_summary: Inserts Articles 5a-5d into Regulation (EU) No 260/2012, requiring PSPs that offer credit transfers in euro to also offer instant credit transfers reachable 24/7 (Article 5a); requiring charges for instant transfers to be no higher than for standard transfers (Article 5b); requiring a free, immediate Verification of Payee service before transfer authorisation (Article 5c); and requiring daily screening of payment service users against targeted financial restrictive-measures lists while prohibiting additional per-transaction screening during execution (Article 5d). Application dates are staggered by PSP type and euro-area status.

notes: Article-level text for 5a-5d confirmed via direct EUR-Lex fetch.
